## Goal

Replace the flat information stack with a compact native hierarchy centered on free-space health, recent growth, monitoring state, and one evidence action.

## Deliverables

- Redesigned SwiftUI status board
- Integrated Agent Access control
- Concise evidence freshness and capacity status
- Explicit presentation state model
- State and accessibility tests
- Light and dark visual evidence

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-220-01` — The popover uses system materials, typography, semantic color, symbols, spacing, and controls to make capacity health and growth assessment the first readable layer without crowding.
- `AC-220-02` — Active, paused, degraded, no-baseline, and error states have concise non-conflicting copy, deterministic actions, appropriate focus order, and VoiceOver labels that do not rely on color alone.
- `AC-220-03` — Light and dark appearance previews and representative narrow-content checks reveal no clipping, ambiguous units, or inaccessible contrast.
- `AC-220-04` — Agent Access appears as a concise native privacy control with clear current state and does not visually compete with capacity health or conflate access with monitoring status.
- `AC-220-05` — The board shows last evidence freshness and database usage versus its cap concisely, with full retained-window and export-inventory detail available in Settings rather than crowding the popover.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-220-01` (visual-and-accessibility-test) — State-matrix unit tests, accessibility inspection, light and dark screenshots, launch smoke evidence, and export-action verification.
